event: Philip Kindred Dick and twin sister Jane are born in Chicago
Placed in premature infant incubator after near-fatal malnutrition
Twin sister Jane Dick dies during infancy from malnutrition at six weeks old
The Dicks live in the Washington, DC area; Edgar Dick continues working as a federal investigator while Dorothy struggles with depression following Jane's death.
notes: Bridge years between Jane's death (Jan 1929) and the parents' separation.

event: Parents Edgar and Dorothy Dick formally separate when Philip is two years old
The Dick family moves briefly to Reno, Nevada during a period of marital strain; the household continues to deteriorate through Dorothy's chronic illness and Edgar's irregular employment.
Divorce of parents Dorothy and Edgar Dick finalized in Washington
Moves with mother Dorothy to Washington, D.C. during early childhood
Enters elementary school in Washington, D.C. at age five

Dorothy and Edgar separate (the formal divorce follows in 1936); Dorothy takes Phil to Berkeley, California, where she settles into the federal civil service work that will support them through Phil's childhood.
notes: The Dorothy/Edgar split is one of the foundational facts of PKD's biography; he sees his father infrequently after this.

event: Dorothy's divorce from Edgar is finalized; Phil enrolls at Hillside School in Berkeley, beginning the elementary education that runs through 1939.
Moves with mother Dorothy to Berkeley, California at age eight
Experiences anxiety and vertigo episodes during elementary school years in Berkeley
Phil's chronic childhood asthma and tachycardia begin to manifest seriously; Dorothy works for the Department of Forestry and the household subsists on her federal salary.
notes: PKD's lifelong tachycardia — variously interpreted by him as cardiac, anxiety-driven, and supernatural — dates from this period.

event: Discovers science-fiction magazines including Stirring Science Stories at age eleven
Reads L. Frank Baum and early fantasy literature during childhood
Begins writing early short stories as a teenager in Berkeley
Reads pulp science fiction by van Vogt, Heinlein, and Sturgeon

Dorothy enrolls Phil at California Preparatory School in Ojai for the autumn term; Phil writes a series of letters to his mother documenting homesickness, the school's mandatory work program, and the early formation of his classical music tastes (Mozart, Brahms, Beethoven, Tchaikovsky).
source: PKD letters to Dorothy K. Dick, Sept-Nov 1942 (Selected Letters Vol. 1)
notes: The Ojai letters are among the earliest substantial PKD prose extant; they document his teenage classical-music obsession including the wishlist of records (Jupiter Symphony, Brahms 1st, Beethoven Emperor) that anchors the music-in-PKD essay.

event: After two months at Cal Prep, Dorothy negotiates Phil's return to Berkeley due to his repeated requests; he resumes Berkeley schooling for the remainder of the academic year.
source: PKD letters to Dorothy K. Dick, Nov 1942

event: Phil deepens his reading at Berkeley public schools, encountering early-childhood favorites that will recur in the Exegesis: A.A. Milne, Wind in the Willows, Pinocchio, and (by year-end) the first science-fiction pulps that he subsequently identifies as the formative encounter with the genre.
notes: PKD locates his first SF pulp encounter (Stirring Science Stories, sometimes Astounding) in this period; the dating is approximate and varies across his retellings.

event: Enrolls at Berkeley High School and participates in creative writing activities
Reads philosophy and psychology independently as a high school teenager
Participates in Bay Area science-fiction fan circles during high school years
Gains first exposure to Platonism and classical Greek philosophy
Attends lectures at UC Berkeley informally after leaving enrollment
Begins working at University Radio Shop record store in Berkeley
Enrolls briefly at the University of California Berkeley before dropping out
notes: Leaves without completing degree

event: Undertakes deep reading in classical music theory and opera history
Begins reading existentialist philosophy including Heidegger and Sartre
Marries Jeanette Marlin in his first brief marriage at age nineteen
Reads Freud and early psychoanalytic literature during late teens

Phil works steadily at University Music on Telegraph Avenue in Berkeley, advising customers on classical recordings and absorbing the catalog knowledge that he will draw on throughout the fiction; he attends UC Berkeley briefly without completing a term.
source: Sutin; Anne R. Dick (The Search, on the record-store milieu)
notes: The University Music period (1948–1951) shapes the Mary and the Giant / In Milton Lumky Territory record-store milieu and PKD's classical-music vocabulary.

event: Divorces Jeanette Marlin after a brief and troubled first marriage
Marries Kleo Apostolides in his second marriage in Berkeley
Reads Kant and Schopenhauer intensively during early writing career
Corresponds with other science-fiction writers through pulp magazine networks
Begins selling short stories to pulp science-fiction magazines professionally
Socializes with Bay Area science-fiction writers and active fan community
Writes early science-fiction novels intended for publication by Ace Books
Reads Alfred North Whitehead and process philosophy for the first time
Develops friendship with science-fiction editor Don Wollheim at Ace Books
Receives financial assistance from Robert A. Heinlein during difficult period
notes: Establishes correspondence and borrows money during financial difficulties

event: First novel accepted for publication by Ace Books as paperback original
Reads Stendhal, Flaubert, and Maupassant intensively as literary models
Attempts to break into mainstream literary fiction market with realist novels
Writes several mainstream realist novels that publishers consistently reject
Divorces Kleo Apostolides after five years of marriage in Berkeley
Publishes debut novel Solar Lottery through Ace Books as paperback original
Sustained immersion in classical music and Wagnerian opera during Berkeley years
Immerses in classical music listening and Wagnerian opera appreciation
Marries Anne Williams Rubinstein in his third marriage in the Bay Area
Moves to Point Reyes Station area with Anne in rural Marin County
Reads Carl Jung's psychological works for the first time in depth
Reads Martin Buber and Jewish theological writings on dialogue and faith
Experiences nervous breakdown and psychological crisis in Point Reyes Station
Writes several mainstream realist novels that remain unpublished during his lifetime
entities: The Man Whose Teeth Were All Exactly Alike

event: Develops growing interest in Gnostic religious thought and ancient heresies
Moves to rural Marin County property with Anne and stepdaughters
Reads works of Plato and Neoplatonist philosophers including Plotinus
Daughter Laura Archer Dick born to Philip and Anne in Marin County
Reads Taoist texts including the Tao Te Ching and Chuang Tzu
Studies the I Ching divination system and uses it as compositional method
notes: Used while writing The Man in the High Castle

event: Publishes The Man in the High Castle through Putnam as hardcover edition
entities: The Man in the High Castle

event: Divorces Anne Williams Rubinstein after seven years of marriage
Wins the Hugo Award for Best Novel for The Man in the High Castle
entities: The Man in the High Castle

event: Marries Nancy Hackett in his fourth marriage in the Bay Area
Reads early Christian theology and patristic sources including Augustine
Engages with Bay Area counterculture intellectual scene in the mid-nineteen-sixties
Writes The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch during a prolific period
entities: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch

event: Increasing amphetamine use during an extremely prolific writing period
Develops interest in mysticism and comparative religion across traditions
Divorces Nancy Hackett after a short and difficult fourth marriage
Reads works of Teilhard de Chardin on evolution and theology
Reads existential theology of Paul Tillich and systematic theology texts
Briefly remarries Nancy Hackett before a second and final separation
Moves to the San Rafael area in Marin County north of San Francisco
Develops friendships with Bay Area SF writers including K. W. Jeter
Expands reading in philosophy of time, metaphysics, and ontology
Experiences increasing paranoia alongside continued amphetamine drug use
Participates in Berkeley and Marin counterculture social circles during late sixties
Publishes Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep through Doubleday
entities: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

event: PKD drafts the Maze/Tench theology notes that develop the colony plot, Delmak setting, divine plurality, the Manufacturer, decay, and the form-destroying principle later associated with A Maze of Death.
source: The Maze of Death Theology (Maze notes PDF)
notes: Entered as an early Exegesis-adjacent primary document. The Sarill/multiple-universes/Wheeler lead remains a source-confirmation task.

event: William Sarill first meets PKD and later spends more than a month as his houseguest during the period associated with the theology behind A Maze of Death.
source: William Sarill, Will the Real Ubik Please Stand Up?; A Maze of Death foreword
notes: Sarill confirms the 1968 meeting and extended houseguest period; PKD's Maze foreword credits Sarill as co-developer of the abstract religious system behind the novel.

event: Writes that he and Roger Zelazny are planning to collaborate on Deus Irae from a 1964 outline Dick had been unable to complete alone.
source: Selected Letters Vol. 1, letter to Andy, May 21, 1968
notes: Letter id: LET_1968-05-21_ANDY_0140.

event: Reads Eastern religious texts including the Bhagavad Gita and Buddhist writings
Publishes the novel Ubik exploring themes of entropy and false realities
Discusses theology and mysticism with Tim Powers and other young writers
Begins intense study of early Christianity and its origins in antiquity
Separates from Nancy Hackett after escalating marital problems in San Rafael
Separates from Nancy Hackett amid escalating marital conflict in San Rafael
During the period of strongest paranoia around the San Rafael break-in, Arnold treats amphetamine use rather than LSD as the more plausible drug context for Dick's paranoid episodes.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Arnold emphasizes long-term speed use and cautions against over-attributing Dick's paranoia to LSD.

event: Home in San Rafael burglarized under mysterious and never-resolved circumstances
Hospitalized for psychiatric evaluation related to paranoia and depression
Develops paranoid theories about government surveillance of his household
Reads Gnostic texts and Nag Hammadi library materials in translation
Meets Tessa Busby in Fullerton, California after returning from Vancouver
Returns to the United States from Canada and settles in Orange County
Attempts suicide while living in Vancouver and is hospitalized afterward
Moves to Vancouver during a period of deep personal crisis
After the Vancouver convention and a suicidal crisis, Dick enters the X-Kalay residential addiction-treatment community.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Arnold frames X-Kalay as central to the post-Vancouver drug and recovery period.

event: Delivers his first major public lecture at the University of British Columbia's Faculty Club in Vancouver, launching the public lecture circuit that later leads to more university appearances.
location: University of British Columbia, Vancouver, British Columbia

event: Son Christopher Dick born to Philip and Tessa in Fullerton
Marries Tessa Busby in his fifth and final marriage in Fullerton
Records a talk at California State University, Fullerton with Willis E. McNelly, part of the university archive relationship that grows into the manuscript collection at CSUF.
location: California State University, Fullerton, Fullerton, California

event: Develops fascination with messianic and prophetic religious traditions in reading
Begins writing the Exegesis notebooks as ongoing theological journal
Arnold reconstructs the doorstep pharmacy delivery in which a dark-haired woman wearing a gold fish pendant triggered the fish-sign anamnesis at the start of 2-3-74.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Arnold compares Dick's account with Tessa Dick's account and flags discrepancies in the fish-sign recognition scene.

event: Reports first pink light visionary experience during dental recovery at home
notes: Defining 2-3-74 event. Multiple old entries consolidated.

event: Reports telepathic messages and visions of ancient Rome over several weeks
Reports vision that reveals undiagnosed inguinal hernia in infant son Christopher
Develops concept of Zebra as cosmic intelligence behind his visions
Arnold summarizes Dick's reports of red-and-gold plasmatic energy that seemed alive, holy, wise, and both inside and outside him during the 2-3-74 aftermath.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Useful for the biography's religious-experience lane and for cross-linking to theophanies.

event: Arnold tracks the return of Dick's female AI voice in semi-conscious states, later interpreted by Dick as a divine feminine guide associated with Sophia.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Connects the high-school physics-exam voice to post-2-3-74 religious interpretation.

event: Interprets recurring dreams as encoded theological messages from a higher source
Begins systematic philosophical speculation on the nature of time and reality
Develops Black Iron Prison theory and hidden Roman Empire concept in Exegesis
Writes thousands of pages of theological speculation in the Exegesis journals
Separates from Tessa Dick after two years of marriage in Fullerton
Writes John Brunner about a London Times clipping on CIA break-ins and says it matches the method of the unresolved November 1971 San Rafael break-in.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to John Brunner, January 14, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-01-14_JOHN_BRUNNER_0011; important SF-author correspondence plus break-in evidence.

event: Tells Lurton Blassingame that A Scanner Darkly is based on three years of research and predicts it will win major awards.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Lurton Blassingame, April 5, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-04-05_LURTON_BLASSINGAME_0087.

event: Writes Ursula K. Le Guin about The Lathe of Heaven, his absent London speech, and the relationship between her dream-universe fiction and his own false-reality experiences.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Ursula Le Guin, April 17, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-04-17_URSULA_LE_GUIN_0097.

event: Reports to Nancy and Isa Hackett that Roger Zelazny has finally mailed his completed Deus Irae material, making a full rough draft available.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Nancy and Isa Hackett, July 2, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-07-02_NANCY_ISA_HACKETT_0107.

event: Writes that he has spent sixteen months and more than a thousand dollars researching Christianity for the planned novel To Scare the Dead.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Goran Bengtson, July 10, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-07-10_GORAN_BENGTSON_0114; a key bridge from 2-3-74 into VALIS-related writing.

event: Tells Lawrence Ashmead that he borrowed $1,700 from Robert A. Heinlein to pay income taxes and wants to repay him from the Scanner advance.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Lawrence Ashmead, August 18, 1975
notes: Letter id: LET_1975-08-18_LAWRENCE_ASHMEAD_0135.

event: Corresponds with scholars and writers about theology, philosophy, and mysticism
Completes early drafts of VALIS-related material drawn from the Exegesis
Objects that Harlan Ellison's Dangerous Visions note claiming he wrote 'Faith of Our Fathers' during an LSD trip is untrue.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Sharon Jarvis, January 13, 1976
notes: Letter id: LET_1976-01-13_SHARON_JARVIS_0199; useful for separating reputation from self-report about drugs.

event: Recalls Robert A. Heinlein warning him that Orange County smog and lifestyle stress could kill him.
source: Selected Letters 1975-1976, letter to Mike Bailey, May 25, 1976
notes: Letter id: LET_1976-05-25_MIKE_BAILEY_0255.

event: Develops theory of living information and cosmic mind in the Exegesis notebooks
Conducts sustained study of Gnosticism and early Christian heresies in depth
During severe late-1970s depressive episodes, friends enlist Joan Simpson to help care for Dick, whose apartment is cluttered with papers, snuff cans, and medication bottles.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Adds one of the requested women/relationships not yet represented in curated biography.

event: At the 1977 Metz science-fiction convention in France, Dick publicly discloses 2-3-74 and describes it as a breakthrough to the real world behind appearances.
source: Arnold, The Divine Madness of Philip K. Dick
notes: Arnold notes that some friends feared the appearance signaled a downward spiral.

event: Publishes A Scanner Darkly drawing on his drug culture experiences

Writes Julian Jaynes after reading The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, praising the theory and comparing Jaynes's divine-voice model to his own March 1974 right-hemisphere/Zagreus experience.
entities: The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Julian Jaynes, March 16, 1977
notes: Short quotations to foreground in display: "raving about it" and "Zagreus awaken in my right hemisphere." Letter id: LET_1977-03-16_JULIAN_JAYNES_0021.

event: Explains Jaynes's bicameral-mind theory to Mark Hurst and folds it into his developing VALIS/Zebra model of divine command voices.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Mark Hurst, March 17, 1977
notes: Letter id: LET_UNDATED_MARK_HURST_0023.

event: Tells Carl Bennett that Jaynes's book provides scientific support for aspects of his Zebra speculation and right-hemisphere theory.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Carl Bennett, March 30, 1977
notes: Letter id: LET_UNDATED_CARL_BENNET_1_0025.

event: After several years without contact, PKD encounters William Sarill again and discusses how their theologies have changed since the Maze of Death period.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Eugene Warren, July 28, 1977
notes: PKD writes that the encounter occurred the night before Warren's article arrived; he links Sarill to the theology in Maze and then describes his 1974 Trinitarian conversion.

event: Writes Eugene Warren that Star Wars has religious importance because it makes Christian mystery available through popular science-fiction imagery, comparing Obi-Wan's voice to the voice he heard when VALIS took him over in March 1974.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Eugene Warren, October 2, 1977
notes: Short quotations to foreground in display: "mystery of our religion" and "Word and Hand of God." Letter id: LET_1977-10-02_EUGENE_WARREN_0043.

event: After returning from the Metz convention, writes Claudia Bush about the reception of his theology-heavy speech, a French romantic fixation, and seeing Star Wars.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Claudia Bush, October 3, 1977
notes: Letter id: LET_1977-10-03_CLAUDIA_BUSH_0038.

event: Develops VALIS theology as systematic framework in the Exegesis notebooks
Intensifies Exegesis writing with expanded theological and cosmological speculation
Writes Patricia Warrick that his right hemisphere dictates while the left types, says he wrote Jaynes about the experience, and dates the disinhibition of the right brain to March 15, 1974.
source: Selected Letters 1977-1979, letter to Patricia Warrick, June 13, 1978
notes: Letter id: LET_1978-06-13_PATRICIA_WARRICK_0100.

event: Reads scholarly works on mysticism, religious psychology, and altered states
Delivers public lectures discussing mystical experiences and theological ideas
Moves to a new apartment in Orange County during his later writing period
Maintains extensive correspondence with fans about metaphysics and religion
Receives increased attention from Hollywood studios for film adaptations of novels
Deepens Exegesis reflection on simulation theory and the nature of reality
Visits the Blade Runner film production set and meets director Ridley Scott
Publishes The Divine Invasion as the second novel in the VALIS trilogy
Incorporates religious visions into late novels including The Divine Invasion
Writes Russell Galen while planning The Owl in Daylight that Jaynes's bicameral model and his own android/type-A theory have led him to a possible 'Type C' evolutionary psyche.
source: Selected Letters 1980-1982, letter to Russell Galen, July 16, 1981
notes: Letter id: LET_1981-07-16_RUSSELL_GALEN_0105.

event: Suffers a major stroke at home leading to hospitalization in Santa Ana
Philip K. Dick dies at age fifty-three following a series of strokes
Sustained reading of Carl Jung's analytical psychology and archetypes theory
